description: The one operating point shared by the controller, every scenario and every baseline config. None of them keeps its own copy of these values; they name an entry here (see experiments/controller/operating_point.py). Derived entries are recomputed from the profile file when the controller starts and a mismatch stops it.
shared_profile_note: Every arm, fairbind and baseline, is compared at the data-api-fast-v1 values. The open-weights column is used only by a run started with --profile-name open-weights-standard-v1.

v_atomic.source: profile maxPurchaseValue; equals the measured median price (prices.median_price_atomic)

h.source: honest verifier bond share assumed by the profile; not measured

beta.source: predicate false-pass rate; placeholder until measured

alpha.source: predicate false-fail rate; placeholder until measured

c.source: rate at which a dishonest verifier issues a wrongful FAIL

p_ceiling.source: profile effectivePpm / PPM; set at or below the bound pi * (h * (1 - beta))^2

L_blocks.source: judgmentDelayBlocks = the longest case path L_F (profile-v1 section 3, ADR 0024): the latest opening, including a sample case opened after a buyer non-delivery dispute ended as delivered, every stage with all its assignments and serve procedures, two lapsed review seals, and the block in which a stalled seller-appealed review upholds the initial FAIL

delta_F_blocks.source: worst-case delay from a bad settlement to the freeze at its initial FAIL under freezeOnInitialFail = true (the override build used by the deferral sweep) = openHorizon + maxAssignments * (judgeBlocks + 1) + evidenceBlocks; a production profile (freezeOnInitialFail = false) freezes at the confirmed failure, at most L

L_min_blocks.source: lower bound on that delay whatever the seller does = epochBlocks + anchorBlocks + beaconDelayBlocks

L_actual_blocks.source: blocks from the settlement of a sampled bad sale (first block of its epoch) to its confirmed failure (FINAL(FAIL), bond frozen, claim window open), keeper delay excluded, on the worst judgment path of experiments/controller/worstpath.py with every actor at the last admitted block: sampled, opened at the end of the open window, every assignment of every stage redelivers through serve, challenge and publication at their deadlines; in the initial stage the first two assignments deliver FAIL at the judge deadline, evidence is requested at the appeal deadline and the assignment is voided by timeoutEvidence in the block after the evidence deadline, the last one delivers FAIL, evidence is requested at the appeal deadline and disclosed at the evidence deadline and the seller appeals at the renewed appeal deadline; in the review stages all but the last assignment time out at the judge deadline; each review seal lapses once. value is the largest and min the smallest over the measured effective-detection cases (the positive controls use min, M4-worst uses value); the contract path is deterministic, so they are equal. Measured on the contract by contracts/test/WorstPathLength.t.sol:test_worstPath_dataApi; caseHorizon - marginBlocks - L_actual = 893. Shorter sampled variant measured by the same file: non-last initial assignments time out at the judge deadline (25480). A case opened by a buyer WRONG_DELIVERY dispute at the end of the claim window of an unsampled sale is not a sampled path and is recorded apart (29672). Reproduced by the service harness dry run (services/internal/integration/worstpath_test.go, TestWorstPathDirectiveDataAPI): every service carries out the worst-path directive on Anvil; the one effective-detection case gives case_path_minus_keeper 29680 with keeper_delay_budget_blocks 0 (L 29680) and 100 (L 29780, keeper_delay_sum_blocks 100), so the dry-run min and max equal the contract value.

L_enumerated_longest_blocks.source: longest path from a settlement to a confirmed failure over every case path the contract admits, enumerated by experiments/case_paths.py with every actor at the last admitted block and prompt public calls (ADR 0024): a buyer NON_DELIVERY dispute opened at the earlier of claimUntil and the sample-open deadline ends as delivered at the publication deadline, the sample case opens in that block, and the seller-appealed tiebreak stalls, which upholds the initial FAIL; equal to judgmentDelayBlocks and measured by contracts/test/WorstPathLength.t.sol test_longestPath. A documented variant only: no scenario symbol reads it and it does not replace L_actual_blocks, which the services' worst-path directive drives.

keeper_margin_blocks.source: hold_period - caseHorizon: the blocks by which keepers may be late at every step of a case before a release could precede the confirmed failure (with the horizon of ADR 0024)

hold_period_blocks.source: profile deferBlocks = retentionBlocks = claimWindowBlocks = failureWindowBlocks = inconclusiveWindowBlocks, kept at the value chosen before ADR 0024, above caseHorizon

failureLimit.source: profile failureLimit (per-settlement wrongful final failure bound over failureWindowBlocks + caseHorizon with u = 3 * w1^2; profile-v1 section 4); a failure window opened at scale factor n sanctions at n * failureLimit (ADR 0021)

lambda_max_per_block.source: profile maxRatePpmPerBlock / PPM, per unit of sellerPenalty in the bond account

refill_per_block.source: profile refillPpmPerBlock / PPM, per unit of sellerPenalty

bucket_capacity.source: profile bucketCapacity, per unit of sellerPenalty

g_over_p_atomic.source: g * ceil(1 / p_ceiling) = expectedPenaltyFloor at D >= L

rates.dataset: Dune, Base USDC transferWithAuthorization calls through 20 facilitator addresses, 2026-09-08 to 2026-09-22 (14 days), 683,553 settlements, 4,400 receiving addresses (queries 8803478 and 8803526)
rates.unit: settlements per hour; the controller converts to settlements per block with chain.block_seconds

top_seller_14d_mean.source: 14-day mean rate of the receiving address with the most settlements (all hours of the 14 days in the denominator)

top_seller_active_hour.source: mean rate of the top address over the hours in which it settled at least once, as reported with the same dataset; its own peak hour is 1,458 per hour (ratio about 2.7). It is below that address's 14-day mean, so the two were computed over different hour sets; recompute from the hourly series before relying on it

top_seller_peak_hour.source: highest one-hour count of the address with the most settlements

mean_14d_p99_top400.source: 99th percentile of the 14-day mean rate within the 400 addresses with the most settlements (percentiles_within_top_400.mean_14d_per_hour.p99); the middle rate level of the I6 grid

peak_hour_p99.source: 99th percentile over all 4,400 addresses of each address's highest one-hour count; the default percentile for bucket capacity

peak_hour_max.source: highest one-hour count of any address

percentiles_within_top_400.note: Percentiles inside the 400 addresses with the most settlements, not over all 4,400 addresses; the p99 here is near rank 4 of 4,400.

median_price_atomic.source: median settlement amount in the same dataset (0.01 USDC)

replaced_values.note: Values carried by the earlier shared baseline constants that conflicted with this file and are no longer used anywhere.

n_sellers.reason: one day of a third-party payment graph; replaced by the 14-day ledger count of 4,400 receiving addresses

lambda_mean_per_hour_top_seller.reason: one-day mean from the same graph; replaced by rates.named.top_seller_14d_mean

effective_p.reason: earlier h = 0.9 placeholder; replaced by p_ceiling

L_blocks.reason: three-hour placeholder; replaced by L_blocks derived from the profile

g_atomic_and_v_atomic.reason: 1 USDC placeholder; replaced by the profile maxBadGain and maxPurchaseValue

d_sweep_points_blocks.reason: replaced by the deferral grid in experiments/scenarios/README.md
